does: Cooks cut vegetables in spiced fat with no added water, under a lid over a low heat, so that they soften in their own steam and end up coated in a thick spiced paste, with no gravy left in the pan.
how: Cut the vegetables into pieces of an even size and pat them dry.
Start the pan with a tempering of whole spices and a masala base cooked until its fat parts.
Add the vegetables and stir until they are coated. Add salt.
Cover the pan and cook over a low heat, lifting the lid and stirring now and then, so that the steam from the vegetables does the cooking. Sprinkle in a spoonful of water only if the pan catches.
Take off the lid at the end and stir over a higher heat for a short time, until any moisture has gone and the spices cling to the pieces.

cues.text: The pieces are tender and coated in a thick, dry spice paste, with a little browned crust on some.
A piece breaks easily under a spoon and a fork goes in with no resistance.

mistakes.mistake: Adding water at the start, so that the vegetables boil and the dish turns into a watery stew.
mistakes.fix: Trust their own moisture and add only a spoonful if the pan catches.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring hard, so that soft vegetables break into mush.
mistakes.fix: Stir gently and seldom, and use a wide pan.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the lid on to the end, so that the dish is damp and not dry.
mistakes.fix: Take the lid off for the end of the cooking and let the moisture cook away.

comes_after.why: The vegetables go into a masala base that has already been fried until its fat parts.

variant_of.differs: No liquid is added, and the pieces are not browned first. The vegetables cook in their own steam under a lid and the dish ends dry, with a coat of spices, and not in a sauce.
